sourceNote.title: Checkout address form
sourceNote.html:
Checkout shipping address

Testing the new shipping address step in a demo web shop (staging build 2.4.0).

  • Fields: full name, street and number, postcode, city, country (dropdown, NL/BE/DE).

  • Postcode format depends on country: NL is 4 digits + 2 letters (1234 AB, space optional), BE and DE are 4 and 5 digits.

  • Name max 60 characters; street max 100.

  • Continue button is disabled until all required fields are filled. Errors show inline under the field after leaving it.

  • Changing country after typing a postcode re-validates the postcode.

  • Observed: pasting a postcode with a trailing space for NL showed an error, typing the same value did not.

  • Observed: the address is kept when going back from payment to shipping.

bodyHtml:
Scope: Checkout shipping address step, demo web shop, staging build 2.4.0. Checklist-based cases derived from the supplied note.

Shared preconditions: Open the shipping address step. Available fields are full name, street and number, postcode, city, and country; country options are NL, BE, and DE.

Scenario: Required fields and inline validation

Test case: Continue requires completed required fields

Purpose: Verify the completion gate.

Preconditions: Shipping address form is open.

Test data: An incomplete address, then a completed address using NL and postcode 1234 AB.

Steps:

  • Leave each required field empty in turn while completing the other required fields; verify Continue remains disabled.

  • Complete all required fields with valid values; verify Continue becomes enabled.

Expected result: Continue is disabled until all required fields are filled.

Coverage notes: The note does not identify which individual fields are required.

Test case: Field errors appear after leaving the field

Purpose: Verify inline error placement and timing.

Preconditions: Country is NL.

Test data: Postcode 123, which does not match the NL format.

Steps:

  • Enter 123 in postcode and leave the field; verify an error appears inline beneath postcode.

Expected result: An inline postcode error appears after leaving the field.

Coverage notes: Exact error wording is not supplied.

Scenario: Country-specific postcode formats

Test case: NL accepts the optional space

Purpose: Verify both documented NL formats and reject an incomplete value.

Preconditions: Country is NL.

Test data: 1234 AB, 1234AB, 1234 A.

Steps:

  • Enter 1234 AB and leave postcode; verify no postcode format error appears.

  • Replace it with 1234AB and leave postcode; verify no postcode format error appears.

  • Replace it with 1234 A and leave postcode; verify an inline postcode error appears.

Expected result: NL accepts four digits followed by two letters, with or without the separating space.

Test case: BE requires four digits

Purpose: Verify the BE postcode length and digit requirement.

Preconditions: Country is BE.

Test data: 1234; invalid values 123, 12345, 123A.

Steps:

  • Enter 1234 and leave postcode; verify no postcode format error appears.

  • Enter each invalid value separately and leave postcode; verify an inline postcode error appears for each value.

Expected result: BE accepts a four-digit postcode; the supplied shorter, longer, and non-digit values produce errors.

Test case: DE requires five digits

Purpose: Verify the DE postcode length and digit requirement.

Preconditions: Country is DE.

Test data: 12345; invalid values 1234, 123456, 1234A.

Steps:

  • Enter 12345 and leave postcode; verify no postcode format error appears.

  • Enter each invalid value separately and leave postcode; verify an inline postcode error appears for each value.

Expected result: DE accepts a five-digit postcode; the supplied shorter, longer, and non-digit values produce errors.

Test case: Changing country revalidates an existing postcode

Purpose: Verify validation uses the newly selected country.

Preconditions: Country is BE and postcode contains 1234.

Test data: Postcode 1234; countries BE and DE.

Steps:

  • Change country from BE to DE without editing postcode; verify 1234 is revalidated as invalid.

  • Change country back to BE without editing postcode; verify 1234 is revalidated as valid.

Expected result: The existing postcode is revalidated whenever country changes.

Coverage notes: The note does not specify the exact timing of error display during a country change.

Scenario: Text field length boundaries

Test case: Full name has a 60-character maximum

Purpose: Verify the name length boundary.

Preconditions: Full name is editable.

Test data: Full name strings containing exactly 59, 60, and 61 letters.

Steps:

  • Enter the 59-character name and leave the field; verify it is within the length limit.

  • Enter the 60-character name and leave the field; verify it is within the length limit.

  • Attempt to enter the 61-character name and leave the field; verify a name longer than 60 characters is not accepted as valid.

Expected result: Full name permits up to 60 characters.

Coverage notes: The note does not specify whether excess input is prevented, truncated, or rejected through validation.

Test case: Street has a 100-character maximum

Purpose: Verify the street length boundary.

Preconditions: Street and number is editable.

Test data: Street and number strings totaling exactly 99, 100, and 101 characters.

Steps:

  • Enter the 99-character value and leave the field; verify it is within the length limit.

  • Enter the 100-character value and leave the field; verify it is within the length limit.

  • Attempt to enter the 101-character value and leave the field; verify a value longer than 100 characters is not accepted as valid.

Expected result: Street permits up to 100 characters.

Coverage notes: The note does not specify how excess input is handled.

Scenario: Recorded postcode entry behavior

Test case: NL trailing space through paste and typing

Purpose: Recheck the recorded difference between input methods.

Preconditions: Country is NL; clear postcode before each check.

Test data: 1234 AB followed by one trailing space, identical for both input methods.

Steps:

  • Paste the test value and leave postcode; verify whether the recorded postcode error appears.

  • Clear postcode, type the identical value, and leave the field; verify whether the recorded absence of an error is reproduced.

Expected result: The recorded observation is an error after pasting and no error after typing the same value.

Coverage notes: This preserves observational evidence. The note does not define the intended treatment of trailing whitespace.

Scenario: Address retention during checkout navigation

Test case: Returning from payment retains the shipping address

Purpose: Verify the recorded address retention behavior.

Preconditions: A completed shipping address allows navigation to payment.

Test data: Record the entered full name, street and number, postcode, city, and country; use NL with postcode 1234 AB.

Steps:

  • Complete the shipping address and select Continue; verify the payment step opens.

  • Go back from payment to shipping; verify all five address field values match the recorded values.

Expected result: The shipping address is retained when returning from payment.

Coverage notes: Preserves the observation supplied in the note; refresh and session persistence are not specified.
